medications.purpose: Treatment of pernicious‑type B12 deficiency anaemia
medications.nice_justification: Standard replacement therapy for B12 deficiency (clinical practice)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg oral once daily, increase to 5 mg after 2 weeks, then to 10 mg after another 2 weeks if tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: Essential hypertension and renal protection in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 / NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive for metabolic syndrome

medications.dose: 20 mg oral nightly (increase to 40 mg after 3 months if LDL‑C target not met)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 advises statin therapy for QRISK ≥10 % or ≥2 metabolic‑syndrome components

medications.dose: 500 mg oral once daily with evening meal, titrate to 500 mg twice daily after 1 week, then up‑titrate to 1 g twice daily as tolerated (max 2 g/day)
medications.duration: Lifelong – monitor HbA1c every 3 months, review renal function annually
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for impaired glucose tolerance when eGFR > 30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: 0.25 mg subcutaneous weekly, titrate to 1 mg weekly after 4 weeks (or 0.5 mg if tolerability issues)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review weight and HbA1c every 3 months
medications.purpose: Weight management and additional glycaemic control in obesity with prediabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/NG28 recommends GLP‑1 RA for BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² (or ≥ 27 kg/m² with comorbidity) to aid weight loss and reduce progression to type 2 diabetes

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined effect on renal function and serum potassium; ACE‑I may raise K⁺ while thiazide may lower K⁺, but renal function must be monitored.
interactions_checked.action: Check serum creatinine and potassium 1–2 weeks after starting ramipril; consider discontinuing hydrochlorothiazide.

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine increases atorvastatin plasma concentration, raising risk of myopathy.
interactions_checked.action: Limit atorvastatin to ≤40 mg daily and monitor CK if muscle symptoms develop.

interactions_checked.interaction: Metformin can reduce B12 absorption, potentially worsening deficiency.
interactions_checked.action: Continue B12 replacement and monitor serum B12/MMA every 6–12 months.

contraindications.reason: eGFR unknown; NICE NG28 contraindicates metformin if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² due to risk of lactic acidosis.
contraindications.alternative: If eGFR <30, consider a DPP‑4 inhibitor (e.g., sitagliptin) and intensive lifestyle intervention.

contraindications.reason: Renal function unknown; ACE‑I dose may need reduction if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m².
contraindications.alternative: If severe renal impairment, use ARB at adjusted dose or focus on non‑RAAS antihypertensives.

contraindications.reason: Baseline liver function tests not available; NICE advises checking ALT/AST before initiating statin.
contraindications.alternative: Obtain LFTs; if ALT >3× ULN, hold statin and investigate.

contraindications.reason: History of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 not documented; contraindicated in these conditions per NICE.
contraindications.alternative: If contraindicated, consider orlistat 120 mg TID with meals.

assumptions_warnings: eGFR, serum creatinine and potassium are not provided – assumed normal for initial ACE‑I and metformin prescribing; must be measured before and after dose changes.
Liver function tests (ALT/AST, bilirubin) are missing – required before starting atorvastatin.
Fasting lipid profile and HbA1c are not available – needed to confirm dyslipidaemia and prediabetes severity.
Current blood pressure reading is not documented – required to confirm uncontrolled hypertension and to set target <140/90 mmHg.
QRISK2/QRISK3 score not calculated – needed to justify statin intensity per NICE CG181.
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statins, or GLP‑1 RA is unknown – verify before prescribing.
Patient’s alcohol intake not recorded – excessive intake may affect liver safety of statin.
treatment_summary: The plan addresses metabolic syndrome by initiating ramipril for hypertension, atorvastatin for dyslipidaemia, metformin MR for prediabetes, and semaglutide for weight management, while continuing existing amlodipine and vitamin B12. Interactions have been reviewed, contraindications flagged pending renal and liver tests, and monitoring intervals defined per NICE CG181/NG28. Lifestyle interventions (diet, exercise, diabetes prevention programme) and regular follow‑up are also recommended.
